issues.description: The solution implementation defines a function named write_pixel (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 19–34) but the exercise and template expect a subroutine named set_pixel (problem describes set_pixel; template provides a set_pixel stub at template_repository/pixel.asm lines 36–38 and calls set_pixel from main at line 147). As a result the solution does not implement the expected symbol set_pixel and is structurally inconsistent with the template and the problem description. This will confuse students (they will see the template stub set_pixel but the solution demonstrates a different function name) and make the provided solution non-compilable/runable against the given template (call to set_pixel unresolved).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution implement the expected subroutine name and signature. Either rename write_pixel to set_pixel in solution_repository/pixel.asm (and keep its behavior) or implement a set_pixel wrapper that calls write_pixel. Ensure the symbol set_pixel exists and preserves the required calling/stack/register behavior so the main code's call to set_pixel resolves and the solution is directly usable with the provided template.

issues.description: The exercise text and the template ask students to implement a subroutine named set_pixel. The solution implementation provides a subroutine named write_pixel (which performs the pixel write) rather than set_pixel. This creates a naming mismatch: students reading the solution or comparing template and solution will be confused about which routine they are expected to implement. Additionally, the solution's main still calls set_pixel (but no set_pixel label is defined), making the intended mapping between problem requirement (set_pixel), template stub (set_pixel) and solution implementation (write_pixel) inconsistent and likely to confuse students.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the subroutine name consistent across all artifacts. E.g. rename the solution's write_pixel label to set_pixel (replace 'write_pixel:' with 'set_pixel:') so the implementation matches the problem statement and template stub. Alternatively, change the template and problem references to write_pixel, but the least disruptive fix is to rename the solution routine to set_pixel so students can directly map the requirement to the implementation.
